critical_bugs: Use of pickle.load() on session data introduces arbitrary code execution risk if .pkl files are tampered with or sourced from untrusted environments.
Unhandled OSError/PermissionError in os.listdir() and file reads could crash the entire analysis pipeline if directory permissions change or paths become invalid during execution.
warnings: Broad except Exception: clauses suppress specific error details, hindering debugging and masking underlying I/O failures.
Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) race conditions exist between os.path.exists() checks and subsequent file operations.
Redundant reading of knowledge_engine_report.txt in multiple sections without caching increases I/O overhead.
recommendations: Replace pickle with a safer serialization format like JSON, MessagePack, or HDF5. If pickle is mandatory, implement cryptographic signature verification before deserialization.
Wrap filesystem operations in targeted exception handlers (OSError, PermissionError) to gracefully skip problematic sessions and continue processing others.
Cache file contents after initial read to eliminate redundant disk I/O and mitigate TOCTOU issues.
Validate session directory names against a strict whitelist regex to prevent symlink-based path traversal attacks.
